disease_label_per_paper: Risperidone-induced neuroleptic malignant syndrome with exceptionally high creatine kinase
presentation_summary: 16-year-old girl developed fever, upper-limb rigidity, reduced consciousness, and CK elevation after 5 days of risperidone 1 mg/day.
Admission temperature was 39.3 C and GCS was 12.
Initial CK was 3844 U/L and later rose to 53467 U/L; creatinine and urea stayed within reference ranges.
Associated abnormalities included AST 203 U/L, ALT 102 U/L, potassium 5.5 mmol/L, calcium 7.3 mg/dL, and neutrophilic leukocytosis.
Risperidone was discontinued; she received lorazepam, antipyretic/cooling measures, hydration, and electrolyte management.

risk_context.source_text_value: Risperidone 1 mg/day had been taken for 5 days before presentation.
The report describes a low fixed risperidone dose and no other medicines.

observations.source_text_value: Recent initiation of risperidone at 1 mg/day
Upper-limb rigidity was present on admission.
Behavioral change, sleeplessness, and reduced GCS

observations.quality_note: Preserved but excluded from ordinary ranking because this individual metabolic alkalosis is not a stable NMS disease-shape feature.

course_observations.source_text_value: CK peak 53467 IU/L on hospital day 5
CK decreased to 182 IU/L on day 21

confirmatory_findings.finding: Final diagnosis in paper was risperidone-induced NMS.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The authors diagnosed risperidone-induced neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Body-fluid cultures were negative and CSF analysis was within normal limits.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Cultures showed no growth; spinal fluid analysis was normal.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Brain CT showed cerebral edema and EEG showed low-voltage poorly defined background.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Neuroimaging and EEG abnormalities were reported during the NMS workup.

quality_warnings: The paper's final drug-causality conclusion and infection exclusion are preserved as confirmatory_findings with use_in_ranking false.
Ordinary ranking evidence emphasizes recent dopamine antagonist exposure, fever, rigidity, altered mental status, CK elevation, hyperkalemia, transaminitis, and leukocytosis.
